title: What training must nursing homes provide under CMS rules?
description: CMS nursing home training under 42 CFR 483.95: required topics, 12 hours a year of nurse aide in-service, compliance and ethics training, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: The Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) requires long-term care facilities in Medicare and Medicaid to run an effective training program for all new and existing staff, contractors and volunteers under 42 CFR 483.95. Required topics include communication, resident rights, abuse and neglect prevention, infection control, QAPI and behavioral health. Nurse aides need at least 12 hours of in-service training a year, including dementia management and abuse prevention.
keyTakeaways: 42 CFR 483.95 covers all new and existing staff, individuals providing services under contract, and volunteers, consistent with their expected roles.
The amount and types of training must be based on the facility assessment in 42 CFR 483.71, which must be reviewed and updated at least annually.
Nurse aide in-service training must be no less than 12 hours per year and must include dementia management and resident abuse prevention training.
Operating organizations with five or more facilities must run mandatory annual compliance and ethics training under 483.85 and 483.95(f).
The 2024 minimum staffing standards were repealed by an interim final rule effective February 2, 2026, but the facility assessment and the training requirements remain in the regulation.
regulator: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), US Department of Health and Human Services
appliesTo: Skilled nursing facilities (Medicare) and nursing facilities (Medicaid) subject to the long-term care requirements in 42 CFR Part 483, Subpart B
All new and existing staff, individuals providing services under a contractual arrangement, and volunteers
Nurse aides (in-service training) and paid feeding assistants (state-approved training)
Operating organizations of five or more facilities (annual compliance and ethics training)

sections.heading: Who must be trained under 42 CFR 483.95?

blocks.text: Every long-term care facility in Medicare or Medicaid must train all new and existing staff, contractors and volunteers, consistent with their expected roles. [42 CFR 483.95](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/483.95) opens: "A facility must develop, implement, and maintain an effective training program for all new and existing staff; individuals providing services under a contractual arrangement; and volunteers, consistent with their expected roles."

The words "consistent with their expected roles" mean the program can differ by role. A volunteer who helps with activities does not need the same depth as a nurse aide, but both are in scope. For readers outside the United States: these requirements apply to facilities participating in the federal Medicare and Medicaid programs. This page cites the Cornell Legal Information Institute mirror of the CFR and states the position as at November 2026.

sections.heading: What topics must nursing home training cover?

blocks.text: Section 483.95 lists nine topic areas that training must include "but are not limited to." Some apply to all staff, some to direct care staff, and some to specific roles.

blocks.caption: Training topics in 42 CFR 483.95 (summary)
head: Paragraph
Topic
Who and what
rows: Effective communications as mandatory training for direct care staff.
Staff educated on residents' rights and the facility's responsibilities under 483.10.
What constitutes abuse, neglect, exploitation and misappropriation of resident property; reporting procedures; dementia management and resident abuse prevention.
Mandatory training on the elements and goals of the facility's QAPI program under 483.75.
Mandatory training on the written standards, policies and procedures of the infection prevention and control program.
A way to communicate the program's standards through training or another practical manner; annual training if the operating organization has five or more facilities.
At least 12 hours per year, including dementia management and abuse prevention, with further content set by performance reviews and the facility assessment.
Paid feeding assistants must complete a state-approved training program under 483.160.
Behavioral health training consistent with 483.40 and the facility assessment.

blocks.text: Mapping these topics against roles produces a [training matrix](/glossary/training-matrix), which is the simplest way to show surveyors that each role receives what the regulation requires. See [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix).

sections.heading: How many hours of in-service training do nurse aides need?

blocks.text: Nurse aides need no less than 12 hours of in-service training per year, and the training must be sufficient to ensure their continuing competence. Section 483.95(g) states that in-service training must:

blocks.title: 42 CFR 483.95(g)
blocks.text: "(1) Be sufficient to ensure the continuing competence of nurse aides, but must be no less than 12 hours per year. (2) Include dementia management training and resident abuse prevention training. (3) Address areas of weakness as determined in nurse aides' performance reviews and facility assessment at § 483.70(e) and may address the special needs of residents as determined by the facility staff. (4) For nurse aides providing services to individuals with cognitive impairments, also address the care of the cognitively impaired."

Twelve hours is a floor, not a target: the primary test is continuing competence. Paragraph (g)(3) also makes the content individual, because it must address areas of weakness found in each aide's performance review. Note that (g)(3) still refers to the facility assessment at 483.70(e), its former location; the requirement now sits in 483.71, and CMS corrected a similar outdated cross-reference in 483.35 in its December 2025 rule.

sections.heading: How does the facility assessment set the amount of training?

blocks.text: The facility assessment determines the amount and types of training each facility needs. Section 483.95 states that a facility "must determine the amount and types of training necessary based on a facility assessment as specified at § 483.71."

Under [42 CFR 483.71](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/483.71), the facility must conduct and document a facility-wide assessment of the resources needed to care for its residents competently during day-to-day operations, including nights and weekends, and during emergencies. It must review and update the assessment as necessary and at least annually, and whenever a planned change would require substantial modification. The assessment must address the staff competencies and skill sets needed for the resident population, and all personnel's education, training and competencies related to resident care. Leadership, including a member of the governing body, and direct care staff must be actively involved.

The practical consequence is that the training plan should be revisited every time the facility assessment is updated. A change in resident acuity or a new specialized service can create a new training need that the previous year's plan does not cover.

sections.heading: When is annual compliance and ethics training mandatory?

blocks.text: Annual compliance and ethics training is mandatory when the operating organization operates five or more facilities. Under [42 CFR 483.85](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/42/483.85), such organizations must include "a mandatory annual training program on the operating organization's compliance and ethics program that meets the requirements set forth in § 483.95(f)," along with a designated compliance officer for whom the program is a major responsibility.

Smaller operating organizations still need a compliance and ethics program and must communicate its standards, policies and procedures "through a training program or in another practical manner which explains the requirements under the program" (483.95(f)(1)). The difference is that annual training is not mandated for them.

sections.heading: Did the repeal of the staffing rule change training requirements?

blocks.text: No. The December 2025 repeal removed the minimum staffing standards, not the training rules or the facility assessment. CMS's [2024 final rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2024/05/10/2024-08273/medicare-and-medicaid-programs-minimum-staffing-standards-for-long-term-care-facilities-and-medicaid), effective June 21, 2024, added minimum staffing standards and relocated the facility assessment requirements to 483.71. The [December 3, 2025 interim final rule](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2025/12/03/2025-21792/medicare-and-medicaid-programs-repeal-of-minimum-staffing-standards-for-long-term-care-facilities), effective February 2, 2026, repealed provisions of the 2024 rule because a public law precludes HHS from implementing, administering or enforcing certain provisions until September 30, 2034.

The 2025 rule refers throughout to "the facility assessment required at § 483.71", and both 483.71 and 483.95 remain in the CFR as at November 2026. Facilities should keep their training program tied to a current, annually reviewed facility assessment.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each 483.95 topic to the facility's policies, the roles that must complete it, and the assessment points that show competence, and records which facility assessment version each training plan was based on. When the assessment changes, the affected roles and content can be identified from those links. See how this works for [healthcare and life sciences organizations](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Do contractors and agency staff need nursing home training?
faqs.a: Yes. Section 483.95 covers individuals providing services under a contractual arrangement, as well as employees and volunteers, consistent with their expected roles. Facilities using agency staff should be able to show that those individuals received the training their roles require, whether the facility or the agency delivered it.

faqs.q: Is there a required number of training hours for staff other than nurse aides?
faqs.a: Section 483.95 sets a specific hour minimum only for nurse aide in-service training, at no less than 12 hours per year. For other staff, the amount and types of training must be based on the facility assessment and be consistent with their roles. State licensing rules may add requirements.

faqs.q: Must dementia training be repeated every year?
faqs.a: For nurse aides, yes in effect: the annual in-service training under 483.95(g)(2) must include dementia management training and resident abuse prevention training. For other staff, 483.95(c)(3) requires training on dementia management and resident abuse prevention, with frequency set by the facility's program and assessment.

faqs.q: Does the training rule apply to assisted living?
faqs.a: Not as such. 42 CFR 483.95 applies to long-term care facilities participating in Medicare or Medicaid as skilled nursing facilities or nursing facilities. A setting that is not certified in either category falls outside this regulation, so its training requirements need to be checked under the applicable state rules instead.
